newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends five cents up as shorts cover.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends five cents up as shorts cover.

text.p: IPE October Brent ended its session high on Thursday on a burst of short-covering before the close and traders said expectations of tighter supplies in the months ahead were behind firmer prices.
October last traded at $22.17 a barrel, up 5 cents on Wednesday's close and just off the daily high of $22.22.

"A lot of people expected the market to fail to hold onto these high levels. There is a lot of length but it is not just outright length, it's long at the front and short at the back so it's more protected," a futures trader said.
"A lot of shorts are giving up and starting to cover and the strength in products is not giving much comfort so that's what's keeping us high," he added.
Short-covering on NYMEX also pushed gasoline prices to a session high near the end and pulled the oil complex with it.
IPE prompt gas oil also extended a late rally shortly before the close. Buyers moved in strongly on the front month ahead of today's options expiry.
Many buyers, and one Wall Street trader in particular, were expecting a shortage of 0.2 percent sulphur gas oil to cover deliveries to the screen.
Sept gas oil closed up $5.25 at $213, Oct settled up $1.50, widening the Sep/Oct backwardation to $9 a tonne.
The European gas oil pool, currently 0.2 percent sulphur for both heating oil and diesel, will be split 60:40 into 0.2 percent for heating oil and 0.05 percent for diesel from Oct 1.
The IPE contract will continue to specify only 0.2 percent.
